observations.body: Daniel (Greek) 5:9–22 identifies a qualified or nonhuman spirit within a scene where it is hardened; the wording centers on “There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods.”

payload.posture: Read Daniel (Greek) 5:9–22 as evidence about the Spirit, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: The passage states daniel (Greek) 5:9–22 identifies a qualified or nonhuman spirit within a scene where it is hardened; the wording centers on “There is a man in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods.” It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of the Spirit.
